en: A state that is without conflict (*araṇa*) and without condition (*appaccaya*) is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a state that is neither with-conflict (*nasaraṇa*) nor without condition. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] to one case each regarding the object, the predominance, and the decisive support conditions.
A state that is without conflict and unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither with-conflict nor unconditioned. (Abbreviated.)
One [condition] by way of object, predominance, and decisive support.
A non-conflict and visible phenomenon is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-conflict and invisible phenomenon.
A non-conflict and visible phenomenon is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-conflict and invisible phenomenon.
Two with respect to object, one with respect to predominance, two with respect to decisive support, prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance.
